To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the MPPs for Schroeder-phase masker complexes were flatter for listeners with hearing impairment than for listeners with normal hearing and that the MPP shapes were influenced by probe level and by the temporal position of the probe relative to masker onset.
the masking period patterns of Schroeder-phase harmonic maskers depend upon the phase of the masker relative to the probe, the level of the probe, and the hearing status of the listener.

the shape of the masked-threshold MPPs is affected by the shape of the internal response generated by the masker, by the level of the probe, and by the presence and absence of a portion of the internal response that is similar in both frequency and temporal position to the probe.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of hearing impairment and stimulus parameters on the ability to detect a probe tone in the presence of a masker.
the role of the cochlear amplifier in masking and the influence of hearing impairment on masking.
the effects of hearing impairment and stimulus parameters on auditory temporal resolution as measured by the masking period pattern.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MPP is a complex function of the interaction of the probe and the masker and the interaction of the masker and its internal representation.
the MPPs for the 60-dB SPL probe level were highly modulated for normal hearing subjects and less so for hearing-impaired subjects.
the masking period patterns of the hearing-impaired listeners were flatter and the masking level differences were lower than those of the normal-hearing listeners.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MPP is a useful tool for investigating the effects of hearing impairment and masker characteristics on the temporal processing of complex tones.

, when the masker is presented at a level above the level at which it is in phase with a probe frequency, then a probe is most difficult to detect if its phase is in phase with the masker at a frequency similar to the probe frequency.
the MPPs obtained in our experiments are a function of the interaction of the probe signal with a particular portion of the maskers' internal waveform.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for normally hearing listeners, the temporal fine structure of a harmonic complex is an important cue to the location of the complex's fundamental.
the MPPs for harmonic maskers are highly dependent on the level of the probe and the hearing status of the listener.
MPPs for harmonic complexes are highly modulated, even for maskers that are not spectrally similar to the probe.
